NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday asked the Centre to examine the institutionalisation of the entire NEET process after it was informed that a panel led by Nandan Nilekani - set up to suggest structural reforms in India's examination system - is likely to submit its first interim report by the end of this month.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told a bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe that the Nilekani-led panel had held exhaustive consultations with members of an earlier committee headed by former ISRO chairman K Radhakrishnan.The top court also asked the joint secretary of the Department of Personnel and Training, who is assisting the Nilekani panel, to file an affidavit detailing the steps taken so far.The bench told Mehta that the government must focus on institutionalising the entire process of conducting the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET).“You must know that permanency of the entire system is key. There should be a permanent setup, permanent staff, permanent verticals. Very less deputation should be there. Only then a permanent structure will come up,” the bench said.Justice Narasimha also said that he and Justice Aradhe would like to visit the newly upgraded facility of the National Testing Agency (NTA) to examine its systems.On August 19, the Supreme Court, observing the need to institutionalise reforms in the NTA, had directed the Centre to inform it about the steps taken to implement the recommendations of the Radhakrishnan panel and the Nilekani committee.The apex court was hearing a batch of petitions, including one filed by advocate Tanvi Dubey on behalf of the Federation of All India Medical Association (FAIMA).
Article Summary: The Supreme Court has asked the Centre to examine the institutionalisation of the entire NEET process. A panel led by Nandan Nilekani is likely to submit its first interim report by the end of this month. The top court also asked the joint secretary of the Department of Personnel and Training to file an affidavit detailing the steps taken so far.

Article Title: FSSAI flags Nestle infant products over false promotional claims, biotin levels
Article Text:
FSSAI said it examined the products and their promotional material available on e-commerce platforms.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) on Friday initiated legal action against Nestle India over alleged non-compliance involving its NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 and Lactogen Pro 1 infant nutrition products.FSSAI said it examined the products and their promotional material available on e-commerce platforms. In the case of NAN Excella Pro Stage 1, the regulator flagged claims relating to “5 HMOs” and “Whey Protein”. For Lactogen Pro 1, it raised concerns over a claim that the product’s “Whey Protein” was easy to digest.According to FSSAI, both products were found to be in contravention of Regulation 4(2) of the Food Safety and Standards (Foods for Infant Nutrition) Regulations, 2020. The provision restricts promotional claims and material intended to increase the saleability of infant foods. The regulator also cited Section 3 of the Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles and Infant Foods (Regulation of Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 1992, which prohibits their advertisement and promotion.FSSAI said it had sought clarifications from Nestle India regarding the claims.Separately, a sample of a follow-up formula manufactured by Nestle India was found to be sub-standard for its biotin content during laboratory analysis.The sample was sent for re-analysis, but the referral laboratory also found it non-conforming with the prescribed biotin requirement under the 2020 regulations.In view of the alleged violations, FSSAI said three separate adjudication cases have been filed against Nestle India in relation to the products. The action covers both promotional claims and the laboratory finding concerning biotin content.
Article Summary: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India initiated legal action against Nestle India. Alleged non-compliance involving its NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 and Lactogen Pro 1 infant nutrition products. FSSAI said it examined the products and their promotional material available on e-commerce platforms.

NEW DELHI: The press information bureau (PIB) fact check unit on Thursday debunked a social media claim that an Indian Air Force (IAF) MiG-29 fighter jet had crashed during landing due to pilot error. They stated that the video being circulated was footage from a video game.The fact-checking unit warned that the video was being circulated by Pakistani propaganda accounts and called the claim fake.“Pakistani propaganda accounts are circulating a video with the claim that an IAF MiG-29 fighter jet crashed during landing due to pilot error,” PIB Fact Check said in a post on X, adding, “Beware! This claim is #Fake.”The unit said the footage was from War Thunder, a military combat video game featuring aircraft, land and naval vehicles.The video circulating on social media shows a fighter jet crashing while attempting to land, followed by the pilot ejecting and parachuting to safety. The footage was presented online as an actual IAF MiG-29 crash by certain accounts based out of Pakistan.PIB Fact Check urged users to report suspicious content related to the Government of India through its official channels.The claim is part of a recurring pattern of propagandist accounts circulating unrelated military accidents and video-game footage are circulated as evidence of recent events.
Article Summary: Pakistani propagandists run video game footage as IAF crash video, PIB fact check unit says. Article Title: 'It can't be that Hindi will not be taught in Tamil Nadu', SC tells state during hearing on Navodaya schools
Article Text:
‘Chennai shouldn’t alienate Delhi’: SC tells Tamil Nadu to reconsider opposition to Navodaya schools

Tamil Nadu raises language concerns

Court stresses cooperative federalism

State raises financial concerns

Supreme Court refuses to recall land direction

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Tamil Nadu government to comply with its December 15, 2025 order to identify land in every district for establishing Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas, while urging the state and Centre to resolve their differences over the schools through dialogue.A bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and Augustine George Masih also questioned Tamil Nadu's opposition to the three-language policy followed by Navodaya schools and said the state should not view the establishment of the centrally funded institutions as a threat to its existing education system."You have to change your mindset, it can’t be that Hindi will not be taught in the soil of Tamil Nadu," Justice Nagarathna observed during the hearing.The bench also said the people in Chennai should not alienate those in Delhi while stressing the need for cooperative federalism."We are saying in addition to all the good things you’re doing in your State, having something in addition will not bring down your standards. Coming from Delhi, will not lower the standards of Chennai. People in Chennai should not alienate Delhi and vice versa," the Court said.The court granted Tamil Nadu three more months to identify suitable land in each district and directed representatives of the state and Central governments to hold further discussions on the policy for establishing the schools.The matter has been posted for December 14.The case relates to Tamil Nadu's challenge to a Madras High Court direction to establish Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district.Navodaya schools are centrally funded, co-educational residential schools run by the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti under the Union Ministry of Education. Tamil Nadu has opposed their establishment, among other reasons, because the schools follow a three-language policy that includes Hindi, while the state follows a two-language policy.Senior Advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for Tamil Nadu, told the court that the state's objection was not to schools or the teaching of Hindi as such, but to the language policy associated with the Navodaya scheme."It is against the State policy. It supersedes Tamil. This kind of unification is not the purport of the Constitution. It is not a Central government school. It is a school run by a society. There is an adamancy that Hindi must predominate."Justice Nagarathna said the language issue could be discussed between the Centre and the state."If you want Tamil as a second language, it is a matter which can be considered," the Judge said, asking the state Secretary to speak to the corresponding Central government Secretary.Gupta said discussions had already taken place but the Centre had remained adamant about Hindi. He nevertheless agreed to another round of consultations.Tamil Nadu also argued that the judiciary could not compel a state to adopt an optional Central government policy through a mandamus.Gupta submitted that education is in the Concurrent List and that Tamil Nadu has constitutional authority to frame its own education policy. He also argued that the Navodaya scheme was not compulsory.Justice Nagarathna questioned the consequences of individual states refusing to accept Central policies."Education is in the Concurrent List. There has to be cooperative federalism. If each State says that I don't accept your policy, what will happen?" the Judge asked.The bench said Tamil Nadu could continue running its own institutions and following its own syllabus, while Navodaya schools would provide an additional educational option.The court also rejected the argument that the establishment of Navodaya schools would lower Tamil Nadu's educational standards."We are not alienating you and we are not alienating them. Some more type of schools come in your state also which will only enhance the high standard which we are aware of. This is not going to lower your standards. If Navodaya schools were going to lower the standard of education in Tamil Nadu we would have said that irrespective of what you would have said. That is not the case here. It will provide more opportunity," Justice Nagarathna told Gupta."Ultimately everybody must work together," Justice Nagarathna said.Tamil Nadu also raised financial concerns, submitting that the Centre had promised to release Rs 5,000 crore for education but had not done so.Gupta argued that the state could not take on additional financial liabilities when funds under existing schemes had allegedly not been released.Additional Solicitor General KM Nataraj, appearing for the Centre, submitted that the state's primary requirement under the scheme was to provide land, while construction and other expenses would be borne by the Central government.Nataraj said the scheme was at an early stage and construction would take several years, during which the language-related differences could be addressed through discussions.Gupta, however, said around 30 acres of land would be required in each district and that identifying land before deciding whether to accept the policy would create difficulties.The bench clarified that it was not directing the state to acquire land immediately, but only to identify suitable land in its government plan.The Supreme Court had in December 2025 directed Tamil Nadu to identify land required for establishing Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district within six weeks. The state subsequently sought recall of the order.On Thursday, the bench declined to recall the direction and instead granted the state three months to comply.In its order, the bench recorded that Tamil Nadu had cited the change in government and lack of material progress in discussions with the Centre as reasons for non-compliance."Be that as it may, we direct the petitioner to comply with our order of 15.12.2025 in so far as identification of the land necessary to establish the school in each district," the order stated.The bench also directed the Centre and Tamil Nadu to continue discussions on the policy while the state works on identifying the land.Advocates G Priyadarshini and Rahul Shyam Bhandari, appearing for Kumari Maha Sabha, the petitioner before the High Court, argued that Tamil Nadu could not deny students access to free education through Navodaya schools."The Court should not get into this debate," Gupta said during the hearing.Justice Nagarathna responded: "That perception that you are surrendering to the central govt should not be there."
Article Summary: Supreme Court orders Tamil Nadu to comply with its December 15, 2025 order to identify land in every district for Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas. Justices BV Nagarathna and Augustine George Masih also questioned Tamil Nadu's opposition to the three-language policy. The bench also said the people in Chennai should not alienate those in Delhi while stressing the need for cooperative federalism.

Article Title: Kashmir cracks walnut success code, turns to medium-sized, grafted trees
Article Text:
A street vendor sells walnuts on the occasion of the Sayar festival, in Mandi on Wednesday. (ANI Photo)

KOKERNAG: In Gohan village, around 100km south of Srinagar, Shabir Ahmad was among many harvesting walnuts from a towering tree. The work has become increasingly difficult. “My back aches now,” Ahmad said. J&K produces 3.5 lakh tonnes of walnuts annually, around 90% of the country’s total output.Like other villagers, Ahmad had no safety gear and he was proud of it. “We have been doing it for centuries,” said Ahmad, also a clerk at a local court. However, the bravado doesn’t help in harvesting seasons. Dr. Mohd Yaqoob Bhat, a surgeon at Paras Hospital in Srinagar, said Valley healthcare units treat dozens of patients each year after falls from walnut trees, some with serious spinal injuries. “There is no mechanism to address the issue,” Bhat said.Ahmad’s younger brother sold one walnut for one rupee and no two fruits are similar. For generations, Kashmir’s walnut trees have been grown from seeds. J&K and Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology (SKUAST) are now promoting medium-sized, grafted walnut trees to bring greater uniformity and help the produce compete globally amid competition from soft-shelled varieties grown in California and Chile.The initiative aims to replace scattered plantations with organised orchards of known varieties, allowing farmers to grow more trees in the same area and produce walnuts more consistent in size and color.J&K has about 80,000 hectares under walnut cultivation, most of it made up of seedling-origin trees. “When someone plants a walnut seed in the ground, whatever grows becomes a tree. Every tree is a variety of its own,” Ashfaq A. Pandit, professor and head of fruit science at SKUAST, said. This natural variation, once considered an advantage, has become a challenge in the modern market where buyers seek consistent produce.Traditional walnut trees can take about 15 years to bear fruit without using pesticides. Unlike traditional seedling-origin trees, grafted walnuts belong to known varieties.Imtiyaz Ahmad Lone, professor and head of SKUAST’s Walnut Research Centre, said the university released new walnut cultivars and grafting-based cultivation had spread over nearly 90,000 hectares despite lack of subsidies.Farmers argued, however, that the grafted varieties are no match for the traditional Kashmiri walnut. “It is no match in taste. The new varieties are brittle, tasteless. They are a no-show,” Mohammad Sultan, a Pulwama farmer in the business for 50 years, said.Researchers differed. Lone pointed out that grafted trees have early bearing, give faster returns as orchards and nut quality are uniform. “They have higher productivity and better export potential. There is a gradual opportunity to replace unproductive seedling trees,” he said.The transition has impacted walnut woodcraft industries. Walnut trees cannot be cut in J&K without govt permission. The matter was debated in the assembly in March when CM Omar Abdullah opposed a bill allowing landowners to cut walnut trees on private property. Omar defended the restrictions, saying the law served a broader purpose of conserving walnut and chinar trees.
Article Summary: J&K produces 3.5 lakh tonnes of walnuts annually, around 90% of the country’s total output. J&K and Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology (SKUAST) are promoting medium-sized, grafted walnut trees.

Article Title: 'We don't appreciate what we get for free': Omar Abdullah backs UPI fee rollout
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah backed Centre's decision to introduce 0.4 percent merchant discount rate on UPI payments above Rs 2,000, saying that "running a UPI system" is not cheap.While talking to reporters, Omar said that people don't appreciate what they "get for free.""Not everyone is charged. First of all, person-to-person money transfers are not charged. After that, individual consumers will not be charged unless they cross a certain ceiling limit. As far as I understand, running this UPI system is not cheap. It takes a lot of money to run it. And the truth is, we don't properly appreciate what we get for free," J&K CM said."The government should ensure that the general public is not charged these fees. If a company is charged, I have no objection because companies make good money through UPI anyway," he added.This comes after the opposition raised concerns over the rollout of UPI charges, alleging that the cost would ultimately be borne by common citizens.Earlier on Wednesday, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi targeted the centre and accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of putting a on every single person by “taxing UPI".“Modiji has a completely diff concept, he's neither left or right he has decided to completely lie down straight and in front of Donald Trump. He's put a tax on every single Indian person by taxing UPI and giving huge amount op money to the United States,” the former Congress president added.The new MDR will take effect from October 15. However, UPI payments between individuals, including transfers made to friends, will not be charged, according to the Centre.Responding to the critics and concerns over the new framework, the Union finance ministry said banks were asked to ensure merchants do not pass MDR charges on to customers. “UPI application providers are expressly prohibited from imposing platform fees or hidden charges".
Article Summary: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah backs Centre's decision to introduce 0.4 percent merchant discount rate on UPI payments above Rs 2,000. Omar said that people don't appreciate what they "get for free" This comes after the opposition raised concerns over the rollout of UPI charges.

Article Title: Flowers at 10,600ft: World’s highest twin fields unveiled in Leh
Article Text:
Spread across 40 acres at Choglamsar and Stakna, the gardens house more than 25 lakh high-value flowers,

JAMMU/SRINAGAR: On Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 76th birthday, Ladakh Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena inaugurated the world’s highest and India’s largest twin flower fields in Leh, at an altitude of 10,600ft, on Thursday as part of the administration’s efforts to diversify agriculture, build skills and create new livelihood opportunities in the Union Territory.Spread across 40 acres at Choglamsar and Stakna, the gardens house more than 25 lakh high-value flowers, including 24 lakh Lilium and 1 lakh Gladiolus. The Choglamsar field was developed in just two months, with plantation beginning on July 16 and the first blooms appearing in the first week of Sept. At Stakna, nearly 1.4 lakh lilies were planted in Aug, with the first blooms expected by Oct-end.Saxena said the initiative was the first experiment of its size and nature at such a high altitude in Leh, adding that its successful execution could pave the way for replication elsewhere in Ladakh. The gardens will open to the public on Sept 18, with an entry fee of Rs 25 for adults and Rs 10 for children, officials said.Floriculture, as a high-value agricultural activity, can complement traditional farming, increase cultivators’ incomes and create opportunities for employment and entrepreneurship, the LG said. The Choglamsar flower park will serve as a training, demonstration and model floriculture centre for farmers and youth, where Lilium, Gladiolus, Tulips and other ornamental flowers will be cultivated for national and international markets.“The facility will provide exposure to modern cultivation techniques, scientific farming practices and improved post-harvest management, enabling farmers to acquire the knowledge and skills required to take up floriculture at farm and village levels,” Saxena said. “Besides functioning as a recreational and educational space for residents and tourists, it will create an ecosystem where not only flowers, but also knowledge, skills and enterprises can grow,” he added.
Article Summary: Spread across 40 acres at Choglamsar and Stakna, the gardens house more than 25 lakh high-value flowers, including 24 lakh Lilium and 1 lakh Gladiolus. The gardens will open to the public on Sept 18, with an entry fee of Rs 25 for adults and Rs 10 for children.

NEW DELHI: Nudged by Supreme Court to reduce the cut-off percentile for admission to super specialty medical courses to fill around 2,000 vacant seats, Centre Thursday told the court that the qualifying percentile for NEET-SS may go from the existing 50th to 30th for the proposed special stray vacancy round, to be conducted soon, reports Amit Anand Choudhary.SC last week asked govt to reconsider its decision not to reduce the cut-off percentile in order to ensure seats were not wasted. Article Title: "Process being carried out in accordance with prescribed rules": Uttarakhand Govt on proposed procurement of 1320 MW of thermal power
Article Text:
"Process being carried out in accordance with prescribed rules": Uttarakhand Govt on proposed procurement of 1320 MW of thermal power

UTTARAKHAND: Uttarakhand Principal Secretary (Energy) R Meenakshi Sundaram on Thursday issued a clarification on questions raised by some political parties over the proposed procurement of 1,320 MW of thermal power, saying the process is being carried out in accordance with prescribed rules, technical requirements, competitive bidding and approval from the Uttarakhand Electricity Regulatory Commission (UERC).Sundaram said allegations regarding the power procurement process were not based on facts and that the objective was to secure the state's long-term and growing electricity requirements, rather than benefit any particular company.Clarifying the tender process, he said the Model Bidding Document issued by the Union Power Ministry in 2019 was a general model document and that changes were examined based on the technology, location, fuel availability, transportation costs and other circumstances of individual projects.He said suggestions and objections received from bidders during the tender process were examined from technical and practical perspectives, following which necessary proposed changes were placed before UERC.The Commission approved the amendments after detailed deliberations.Sundaram also rejected the perception that power procurement was being awarded to a particular company without competition. He said five companies were found eligible at the Request for Quotation (RFQ) stage and competition had also been maintained during the Request for Proposal (RFP) stage."The final selection will be based on the total tariff quoted through the competitive bidding process," he said.The Principal Secretary said the proposed 1,320 MW procurement was aimed at meeting Uttarakhand's long-term baseload requirement and ensuring continuous and reliable power supply to consumers.He said Uttarakhand's importance as a tourism and pilgrimage destination, along with its environmental sensitivity, had been considered while framing the tender. Since thermal power plants require large quantities of coal, transporting it over long distances could increase costs.The tender therefore allows the plant to be established at any suitable location in the country, enabling companies to quote competitive tariffs after considering fuel availability, transportation costs and other factors.Sundaram clarified that there was no restriction on setting up the plant in Uttarakhand and that any company establishing a plant in the state and offering electricity at a competitive tariff could participate in the prescribed process.On transmission costs, he said the arrangements and associated expenses for supplying electricity to Uttarakhand would be determined according to the tender and tariff conditions. "Therefore, the claim that establishing the plant outside Uttarakhand would automatically result in the entire additional cost being borne by consumers was not correct."He said the actual financial impact on consumers would have to be assessed on the basis of the total electricity tariff.On fixed charges, Sundaram said the Model Bidding Document prescribed a fixed charge ceiling of 70 per cent, with at least 30 per cent remaining as fuel charge. Considering bidders' actual costs, fuel availability and circumstances of potential locations, UPCL proposed increasing the fixed charge ceiling to 75 per cent, allowing the fuel charge component to be kept at up to 25 per cent.He said electricity prices were not evaluated solely on the basis of fixed charges but on the total tariff comprising fixed charges and variable or fuel costs. The proposal was examined and approved by UERC after due deliberation.Sundaram said an increase in the fixed charge ceiling from 70 per cent to 75 per cent did not automatically mean an additional financial burden on consumers, as the final payment would depend on the total tariff quoted through competitive bidding.He said construction timelines had also been prescribed to make the 1,320 MW capacity available in phases, with 42 months prescribed for the first unit and 48 months for the second unit.The Principal Secretary said the option of a joint venture between UJVNL and THDC was also considered to meet the requirement. "However, THDC, a subsidiary of NTPC, is required to follow NTPC's prescribed policies, while its core expertise is in hydropower and Pumped Storage Projects. Expansion into other areas would require necessary approvals from its promoter."Sundaram also clarified that the estimated figure of Rs 1.60 lakh crore to Rs 1.66 lakh crore over 25 years did not represent a one-time payment but the potential total payment over the entire period.He said the state's future power requirement had been assessed on the basis of the Central Electricity Authority's Resource Adequacy Study and that actual payments would depend on the final tariff, power supplied, plant availability and other contractual conditions.Reiterating that the procurement process was not a departmental decision alone, Sundaram said it involved multiple stages, including technical examination, bidder competition, financial evaluation and approval by an independent regulatory authority.He reiterated that the primary objective of procuring 1,320 MW was to secure Uttarakhand's future electricity requirements and not to benefit any particular company. The final selection, he said, would be made through competitive bidding.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand Govt on proposed procurement of 1320 MW of thermal power. "Process being carried out in accordance with prescribed rules," says energy secretary. He rejects the perception that power procurement was being awarded to a particular company without competition. Sundaram says there was no restriction on setting up the plant in Uttarakhand.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday told Tamil Nadu govt that it needed to change its mindset towards teaching Hindi in schools and should thrash out issues with Centre on setting up Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district.As Vijay-led TN govt took the same stand taken by the previous DMK govt, a bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and A G Masih said individual states could not act like countries. "You have to change your mindset, it can't be that Hindi will not be taught on the soil of TN," the bench said.TN has been opposing the setting up of these schools as they follow a three-language policy, including Hindi, which is against the state's two-language policy."We are saying in addition to all the good things you're doing in your state, having something in addition will not bring down your standards... There is an adamancy that Hindi must predominate," he said.Gupta submitted that cooperative federalism would never work in only one direction and such a policy should not be enforced by the court.The bench asked the state to comply with its order and posted the case for further hearing in Dec. SC had last Dec directed TN to identify land required for establishing Navodaya Vidyalayas in each district within six weeks."We are not asking you to acquire land. Article Title: EC accepts TMC split, freezes name, symbol in interim order
Article Text:
EC barred both factions from using party symbol, name in Bengal bypolls

NEW DELHI: Acknowledging the split in All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) — with one faction led by Mamata Banerjee and the other by Arup Roy — the Election Commission on Thursday froze its reserved “flowers and grass” poll symbol until final settlement of the intra-party dispute by the commission.For the purpose of the October 6 assembly bypolls in Rejinagar and Nandigram — where both factions have fielded separate candidates under TMC name — the EC in its interim ruling said both the groups may pick a different party name, including which may have linkage with parent party name AITC, and also choose their respective poll symbol from the list of free symbols notified by the poll panel.The two groups have been asked to furnish to EC by Friday 11 am, three options for names by which they may be recognised by the commission, as well as the symbols to be allotted to the candidates set up by them. The chosen names and symbols may be stated in order of preference, for final approval by EC. Once the new party name and symbol are allotted to the two factions, the concerned returning officers will complete the scrutiny of nominations for the two bypolls.EC, in its interim ruling on Thursday, opined after due consideration of submissions made by both Mamata and Arup Roy factions, that there exist two rival groups in AITC, with each claiming to be the “real” party.“Therefore the matter requires a substantive determination by threcommission under Para 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation & Allotment) Order 1968,” it noted.In order to "place the rival groups on an even keel" and based on past precedents, EC ordered that neither of the two factions shall be permitted to use the AITC name or its “flowers and grass” symbol until termination of the dispute under the Symbols Order.EC’s interim ruling places on record full chronology or the intra-party dispute as well as the submissions made by the two groups — through Mamata Bannerjee and Ritabrata Banerjee and others — since June 22, 2026. The basic contention rests on the Ritabrata questioning the constitutional mandate and authority of the AITC national working committee (NWC) to make key appointments in the party on June 5, 2026. Ritabrata argued that tenure of NWC had expired on 11.02.2025, and that it was his group that later reconstituted NWC on June 22, 2026 with Arup Roy as chairperson. On July 6, Mamata said the claims of rival group were fundamentally flawed and illegal and contrary to the party constitution, which gave NCW a five-year tenure ending in 2027.Derek O Brien, it was underlined, had submitted to EC on 07.03.2026 the amended party Constitution for uploading on the commission website.Both sides have since made several submissions to the EC, both in writing and in person, in support of their claims and countering the claims of the rival group to being the real party. The final set of submissions were made by the Arup Roy faction on Sept 16. Both the factions finally met EC in person on Friday, hours before the commission issued the interim ruling freezing the AITC symbol.The interim order coincided with the scheduled date for scrutiny of nominations. As per rules, if necessitated by circumstances that include a dispute over candidates claiming to be fielded by the same party, the returning officer can delay scrutiny of nominations until almost 11 AM on the scheduled day for withdrawal of candidatures.The commission decides a symbol dispute arising from a split in the party, using its quasi-judicial powers. The rival factions are represented before the EC by senior lawyers who argue the case in in-person hearings scheduled by the commission. Both sides are given an opportunity to present their arguments endorsing their claim over the party name and symbol and to also counter the arguments by the rival side. The hearings in a symbol row often span over months.The commission, after hearing both sides and examining their claims and counter-claims, gives a well-reasoned order recognising one of the factions as the “real" party entitled to use its reserved symbol.Over the years, the EC has decided symbol disputes in parties like the Shiv Sena, NCP, AIADMK, Samajwadi Party, Lok Janshakti Party, etc. In all these cases, the final verdict was preceded by an interim order freezing the reserved symbol of these parties.
Article Summary: EC barred both factions from using party symbol, name in Bengal bypolls. EC: Neither of the two factions shall be permitted to use the AITC name or its “flowers and grass” symbol until termination of the dispute under the Symbols Order.

NEW DELHI: Owners who abandon cattle on highways and expressways could face fines and penalties, with the road transport ministry issuing a standard operating procedure (SOP) to curb the menace of stray cattle and other animals causing road crashes. States and local authorities will initiate “owner-tracing” and take steps to recover applicable fees, fines and penalties from owners.The SOP follows a Supreme Court direction to NHAI to devise a structured mechanism for the safe removal of stray animals from national highways and expressways.The “SOP for Safe Removal of Stray Cattle and Other Animals from NHs/Expressways”, issued this week to highway agencies and state govts, designates NHAI, NHIDCL and state PWDs as nodal agencies for removing stray animals from NHs and expressways. They will arrange their safe transportation to shelters, cattle pounds or gaushalas identified by state govts.The highway agencies will identify and mark stretches where stray cattle and other animals are frequently spotted. They will also arrange and bear the cost of transporting the animals to shelters identified and maintained by state and local authorities.States and local authorities will “maintain cattle-pound records and initiate owner-tracing and action for recovery of applicable fees, fines and penalties under the relevant cattle-trespass legislation”, as per the SOP.State govts are empowered to initiate action under the The Cattle-Trespass Act of 1871 .State govts can invoke provisions of The Cattle-Trespass Act, 1871 against owners. Section 25 provides for recovery of fines imposed for damage caused by cattle trespassing through the sale of the animals involved. This applies whether the cattle were caught while trespassing or later, and whether they belonged to the offender or were merely in their charge when the offence occurred.Though there is no separate official data on crashes and fatalities caused specifically by stray cattle and other animals. However, in 2024, 19,082 crashes and 8,917 deaths were recorded under the “run off the road” category. The road transport ministry has said such crashes could result from excessive or inappropriate speed, driver distraction, misjudging a curve or attempts to avoid a collision with another road user or an animal.

Article Title: AIIMS develops AI tool to help detect breast cancer on mammograms
Article Text:
AIIMS Delhi researchers have developed an AI tool that can act as a second reader of mammograms and flag possible signs of breast cancer, with the technology now transferred to BPL Technologies for further development and deployment.

New Delhi: An artificial intelligence (AI) tool developed by doctors and researchers at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Delhi, can act as a second reader of mammograms and alert radiologists to possible signs of breast cancer.AIIMS on Wednesday transferred the technology to Indian healthcare technology company BPL Technologies Ltd for further development, regulatory approval and deployment in hospitals.The model is designed to support radiologists, particularly in hospitals where doctors have limited experience in interpreting mammograms or breast imaging specialists are in short supply.Dr Krithika Rangarajan, Associate Professor, Department of Diagnostic and Interventional Oncoradiology, AIIMS, said the model was designed as a safety net to reduce the chances of missed cancers.“The idea is to act as a second reader and alert the radiologist to any possible cancer, so that they do not miss cancers on mammography,” she said.The model has been trained completely on Indian data. Rangarajan said it was the first Indian version of a mammography AI model.Developed over around one to one-and-a-half years with initial funding from the Ministry of Education, the model was retrospectively tested on around 3,000-4,000 patients at AIIMS.According to Rangarajan, it showed a 99% negative predictive value at the threshold used in the study. This means that when the model indicated no cancer, it was correct about 99% of the time in that study setting. Performance, however, depends on the threshold used.The AI tool has been deployed at AIIMS for around a year in trial mode and is not being used to make clinical decisions. Patients continue to receive reports from radiologists while researchers assess the AI separately.BPL Technologies will take the model towards a finished product, obtain regulatory clearances and provide technical support for hospital deployment. Rangarajan said it could potentially reach hospitals in around six months, depending on regulatory approvals.The technology transfer took place at AIIMS on September 16 in the presence of institute director Prof Nikhil Tandon and BPL Technologies chief financial officer Ajay Jindal.Prof Tandon said the initiative would help translate academic research into solutions addressing real-world healthcare needs.The key patient benefit could be an additional layer of support in mammogram interpretation, particularly in hospitals with limited access to breast imaging specialists. Wider clinical use will depend on validation and regulatory clearances.
Article Summary: AI tool developed by doctors and researchers at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Delhi. The tool can act as a second reader of mammograms and alert radiologists to possible signs of breast cancer. AIIMS on Wednesday transferred the technology to Indian healthcare technology company BPL Technologies Ltd.

NEW DELHI: The Union health ministry has asked states and Union territories to act against unauthorised stem cell therapy, reiterating that it can be offered as routine treatment only for disease conditions or indications approved by the ministry.In an advisory issued on September 16, the ministry said stem cell therapy for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) must remain restricted to duly approved clinical trials. It must not be offered as routine, standard or commercial clinical treatment.The advisory follows the Supreme Court judgment of January 30, 2026, in which the court issued directions on the use of stem cell therapy for ASD. The ministry has asked states and UTs to circulate the directions to state and district regulatory authorities as well as government and private clinical establishments involved in stem cell research, treatment, promotion or administration.The ministry has also flagged the consequences of violations. Citing the Supreme Court's directions, it said non-compliance can attract professional misconduct, besides action under Sections 32 and 40 of the Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010, including cancellation of registration and penalties.The National Medical Commission (NMC), in an advisory issued on September 5, also reiterated that stem cell therapy can be offered as standard clinical care only for approved indications.It said unauthorised administration, prescription, promotion or advertisement of stem cell therapy beyond approved indications would constitute professional misconduct.The NMC has asked State Medical Councils to examine alleged violations and, where professional misconduct by a Registered Medical Practitioner is established after due process, take appropriate disciplinary action.The health ministry has also reiterated that the regulatory framework governing stem cell research and therapy must be followed, including the National Guidelines for Stem Cell Research, 2017, issued jointly by the Indian Council of Medical Research and Department of Biotechnology.The latest advisory puts the focus on enforcement by state and district authorities. It directs authorities and clinical establishments to ensure that unproven stem cell interventions, including those for ASD, are not offered outside the permitted regulatory framework.
Article Summary: The Union health ministry has asked states and Union territories to act against unauthorised stem cell therapy. The advisory follows the Supreme Court judgment of January 30, 2026, in which the court issued directions on the use of stem cell Therapy for ASD.

Article Title: Disability percentage alone cannot decide PG medical eligibility: NMC
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Disability percentage alone will not determine whether a candidate can pursue a postgraduate medical course, according to new National Medical Commission (NMC) guidelines. The framework makes functional competency, course-specific requirements, reasonable accommodation and patient safety central to assessing candidates with benchmark disabilities for MD, MS and DNB courses.Candidates seeking admission under the Persons with Benchmark Disabilities category must have at least 40% benchmark disability and a valid Unique Disability Identity (UDID) Card. However, the disability percentage recorded on the card cannot by itself determine eligibility. The Medical Assessment Board will independently assess whether the candidate can demonstrate the competencies required for the specific postgraduate course.The guidelines lay down course-specific functional requirements, particularly for specialties involving surgery and other hands-on procedures. These include fine motor skills, bimanual dexterity, mobility, depth perception and hand-eye coordination.However, disability rights advocates have questioned some of these requirements. Dr Satendra Singh of Doctors with Disabilities: Agents of Change said: “The requirement of ‘optimum use of both upper limbs’ and non-recognition of sign language are stark examples of ableist criteria in the guidelines. They appear to treat physical characteristics as proxies for professional competence, rather than assessing whether a candidate can safely perform the essential functions of a speciality, with reasonable accommodation. Such blanket requirements risk excluding otherwise qualified doctors from postgraduate medical education. Eligibility and speciality choice should instead be based on individualised, evidence-based functional assessment, taking into account assistive technology and clinical accommodation.”For several other clinical specialties, the assessment will include abilities such as history-taking, examination, basic procedures and documentation. Candidates may use assistive devices or receive reasonable accommodation, including modified instruments, accessible workplaces and flexible schedules where appropriate.The guidelines specifically state that no candidate should be declared eligible or ineligible solely on the basis of the disability category or percentage. Assessment must be individualised, objective and based on functional ability, while reasonable accommodation and assistive technology must be considered before declaring a candidate ineligible.For candidates with conditions such as autism spectrum disorder, specific learning disorder and intellectual disability, the assessment will consider communication, comprehension, ability to follow and give instructions, structured learning, adaptive functioning and independent functioning, with support where needed.The Medical Assessment Board can declare a candidate eligible, eligible with reasonable accommodation, or ineligible, after considering demonstrated functional competency, the feasibility of reasonable accommodation and assistive technology, the ability to complete the course and patient safety. Assessments must be fair, transparent and free of physical, environmental, communication or attitudinal barriers.For specialties requiring fine motor skills, endurance, depth perception or rapid decision-making, the guidelines say disability percentage alone is insufficient and require functional assessment. The framework aims to promote equality and reasonable accommodation while maintaining academic standards and patient safety. It supersedes earlier NMC and Medical Council of India guidelines to the extent that they are inconsistent with the new framework.
Article Summary: New National Medical Commission (NMC) guidelines lay down course-specific functional requirements. Disability rights advocates have questioned some of these requirements. Dr Satendra Singh of Doctors with Disabilities: Agents of Change said: ‘The requirement of ‘optimum use of both upper limbs’ and non- recognition of sign language are stark examples of ableist criteria in the guidelines'

NEW DELHI: Films depicting consumption or trafficking of drugs will now carry an anti-drug warning, the broadcast ministry notified on Wednesday.According to the guidelines amended under the Cinematograph Act, such movie scenes will carry the warning: "Illicit Narcotics Destroy Health and Guarantees Imprisonment. Say No to Drugs".The move follows a similar direction issued to OTT platforms by the ministry last month, asking them to prominently display the same warning during scenes showing the consumption or use of narcotic drugs. A similar advisory was also issued to private satellite television channels.The latest change marks a departure from the earlier film certification guidelines, under which the central board of film certification (CBFC) was required to ensure that scenes that could "encourage, justify or glamorise drug addiction" were not shown. However, those guidelines did not mandate a specific warning to be displayed on screen.The film certification guidelines set out the principles that the CBFC must follow while examining films for public exhibition under the Cinematograph Act. They were last amended in May 2025, when the government added three age-based parental guidance categories — U/A 7+, U/A 13+ and U/A 16+. Introduced through amendments to the Cinematograph Act in 2023, the categories require parental guidance for children below seven, 13 and 16 years, respectively.The guidelines also require the CBFC to ensure that anti-social activities, including violence, are not glorified or justified, while criminal methods that could encourage offences are not depicted. They also prohibit scenes that encourage, justify or glamorise drug addiction.In addition, the guidelines cover depictions of violence, cruelty and sexual content, as well as material that could affect public order, the security of the State or India's relations with foreign countries.On Wednesday, the Centre also reconstituted the CBFC, appointing actors Preity Zinta, Pankaj Tripathi, Suniel Shetty, Pallavi Joshi and Prosenjit Chatterjee, filmmaker Priyadarshan and Grammy-winning musician Ricky Kej, among others, to the new 18-member board.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Thursday refuted the Centre's claim that five of its members supported the government's decision to introduce a merchant discount rate of 0.4% on UPI payments above Rs 2,000, saying that no such discussion took place during the Parliamentary Standing Committee meeting.In a social media post on X, Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi said that the department of finance did not have any specific proposal on UPI tax when it met members of the finance committee."The Parliament standing committee on finance has not discussed the UPI tax proposal that the Modi government has recently announced," Gogoi said."The department of finance did not have any specific proposal on UPI tax when they met the members of the finance committee. Roll back UPI tax. Stop surrendering, PM Modi."Another Congress MP, Manish Tewari, backed Gogoi and accused the Centre of using the privileged proceedings of the Parliamentary Standing Committee to "score brownie points.""It is unfortunate that proceedings of Parliamentary Standing Committees that are supposed to be privileged are now sought to be used by the government to score brownie points," Tewari said in a social media post."My colleague is correct; no specific proposal qua the recent Merchant Discount Rate - MDR to be levied on UPI transactions from October 15th, 2026, was ever brought before the Parliamentary standing committee of Finance - rate, quantum, amount of fee to be charged, ceiling and exemption slabs, etc.," he added.He also said that concerns were raised by the Opposition over the need and efficacy of MDR on UPI payments during various sittings of the committee."Even on the principle or conceptual basis of MDR as my colleague Gaurav Gogoi points out concerns were raised by members with regard to its need, efficacy, etc., over the course of various sittings of the committee," Tewari said."To claim that a particular measure was supported by ‘certain members’ of the committee is an inaccurate and fallacious characterisation of the confidential proceedings of a Parliamentary Committee," he added.This comes a day after a government functionary claimed that Congress MPs, including former finance minister P Chidambaram and former minister in the UPA government Manish Tewari, supported the government's decision during the parliamentary panel's proceedings.“Why is Rahul Gandhi opposing something his own MPs, including former finance minister P Chidambaram and former minister in the UPA government Manish Tewari, supported within the parliamentary panel?” news agency PTI reported a functionary as saying.According to the report of the standing committee headed by BJP MP Bhartruhari Mahtab, the panel noted its earlier recommendation emphasising that due to the imperative of a viable revenue model, legislative-enabling provisions for a tiered MDR structure have been brought forward.However, the committee remained deeply concerned by the staggering mismatch between the Rs 2,000-crore allocation and the industry's estimated operational cost of Rs 20,700 crore.In the view of the committee, while statutory enablement now exists to permit calibrated MDR on high-value transactions, any delay in notifying and operationalising this framework leaves payment service providers heavily dependent on inadequate subsidies, thereby threatening critical investments in cybersecurity, fraud prevention and network infrastructure.On the incentive scheme for promotion of RuPay debit cards and low-value BHIM-UPI transactions (person-to-merchant), the committee, in its report, observed and recommended: “The Committee notes the massive Rs 2,000 crore budgetary allocation for 2026-27 designed to offset ecosystem costs caused by the zero-MDR policy on RuPay and low-value UPI transactions.“The Committee observes that while UPI is expected to process up to 150 billion transactions per month and add 600 million new users, the current government incentive covers merely 11% of the industry's actual costs and 14% of potential MDR collections, creating a structural funding gap impacting long-term infrastructural investment.”The committee recommended that while the proposed three-year multi-year scheme and cashback components are necessary to democratise digital payments in untapped Tier 3-6 cities, the Department of Financial Services must concurrently explore a self-reliant, tiered revenue model.
Article Summary: Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi said that the department of finance did not have any specific proposal on UPI tax when it met members of the finance committee. NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday hit out at Pakistan at the UN Security Council, saying Islamabad had provided a "permissive environment" to the "architects" of the 9/11 attacks and continues to provide space and support to terror groups such as Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed.Speaking at a UN Security Council meeting, India's Permanent Representative P Harish recalled the 9/11 terror attacks in United States and said al-Qaida leaders Osama bin Laden and Khalid Sheikh Mohammed were eventually found in settled communities in Pakistan rather than "caves or badlands".“The international community supported the global campaign to counter terrorism in the wake of 9/11. Let us not forget, however, that al-Qaida's terror ecosystem established its strategic depth beyond Afghanistan through its affiliates,” Harish said.“The leaders of al-Qaida who conceived and directed these 9/11 attacks did not escape justice in the wilderness of some ungoverned frontier.”The Indian envoy also listed out the names of terrorists found in Pakistan.Bin Laden, who ordered and financed the 9/11 plot, was “tracked down and killed in a fortified compound within a settled, guarded community under Operation Neptune Spear”, he said.Mohammed, “the principal architect of the operation, was found sheltering in an ordinary residential house.Ramzi Binalshibh, who coordinated the hijacker cell after being denied a visa to join them, was sheltering in an urban centre,” Harish said.Senior al-Qaida operative Walid bin Attash, who helped select and prepare several hijackers, was captured separately, while Mustafa Ahmed al-Hawsawi, a key financial and logistical facilitator of the 9/11 operation, was also captured in Pakistan, he said."In each case, these were not fugitives hiding in caves or badlands, they were men who had long evaded detection. Draining this swamp that provided an enabling environment for such monsters of humankind to prosper is important," Harish said, in a thinly veiled reference to Pakistan.Harish also drew attention to what he described as an axis involving Pakistan, al-Qaida and terrorists targeting India."The same permissive environment that sheltered the architects of 9/11 has, in the years since, continued to provide space, support, and impunity to affiliates of al Qaida such as Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed and their like," he said.He said these groups continue to operate under different identities to evade the Council's sanctions, while their terror-training infrastructure continues to operate with impunity.The international community must act against the continued existence of such sanctuaries, he said, "to ensure that more such individuals are not thrust upon any country or its citizens and no one loses family and loved ones".Last week, as the world marked 25 years of the September 11 terror attacks perpetrated by al-Qaida, UN Security Council members, including Pakistan, visited the 9/11 memorial in Lower Manhattan.
Article Summary: India's Permanent Representative P Harish recalled the 9/11 terror attacks in United States. He said al-Qaida leaders Osama bin Laden and Khalid Sheikh Mohammed were eventually found in settled communities in Pakistan rather than "caves or badlands" Harish said these groups continue to operate under different identities to evade the Council's sanctions.

Based on this GMP, the implied listing price is around Rs 1,927 per share, indicating expectations of a moderate listing gain.Brokerages have largely taken a positive view of the National Stock Exchange’s IPO. Priju, Portfolio Manager, Karma Capital sees NSE as a structural growth story, underpinned by the continued evolution of India's capital markets.“In our view, the exchange has the potential to emerge as a steady compounder over the long term and can be a meaningful long-term holding in a portfolio. In the near term, a resolution of the issues around the new closing auction mechanism (CAS) could provide an additional catalyst for the stock. Over a much longer horizon, as NSE's role in India's financial markets continues to deepen, the business is likely to command a valuation multiple more akin to that of a public utility,” he says.Also Read | NSE IPO opens for subscription: From GMP, market cap to status & global comparison - top 10 things to know He also believes that there could be some selling on the listing day as certain pre-IPO investors, including eligible AIFs, can monetise their holdings.“Other pre-IPO shareholders remain subject to a six-month lock-in period. This could create some temporary supply and provide a buying opportunity for long-term investors. The IPO saw 43% subscription on the first day, with institutional participation relatively muted at this stage. Given that QIB participation typically builds towards the end of the issue period, we would expect subscription levels to strengthen as the IPO progresses,” he adds.Analysts point to NSE’s market leadership, strong margins, debt-free balance sheet and expanding investor base as factors supporting the long-term investment case. They also see the IPO as an opportunity to gain exposure to India’s dominant market infrastructure company.However, the valuation remains a consideration. At 42.9 times FY26 earnings, the issue is not inexpensive, while NSE’s earnings are closely linked to trading activity, particularly options. A GMP of 8% indicates positive demand, but does not suggest excessive enthusiasm.
Article Summary: National Stock Exchange of India IPO, India’s second largest till date, enters its second day of subscription with a grey market premium (GMP) of around 8%. On the first day, the issue was subscribed 43% overall, with bids received against the 8.86 crore shares on offer. Retail investors subscribed to 44% of the 4.41 crore shares reserved for them.

Article Title: Yudh Abhyas 2026: India, US troops train with drones, robotic dogs and snipers in Auli
Article Text:
India and the United States engaged in advanced counterterrorism exercises

Indian and US Army soldiers conducted a counterterrorism building-clearance and room-intervention drill at Auli in Uttarakhand on Wednesday as part of Exercise Yudh Abhyas 2026, with assault teams supported by drones, robotic dogs, canines and snipers in a close-quarter operational scenario.According to ANI, citing the Indian Army, the drill was designed to replicate close-quarter operational situations and demonstrated the coordinated employment of specialised personnel and technology during counterterrorism operations. US Army personnel also interacted with the troops and equipment involved in the exercise, the report said.The exercise highlights the growing focus on technology-enabled operations, with unmanned and autonomous systems being integrated with conventional combat elements. The Indian Army's latest drill at Auli brought together assault teams, snipers, canines and robotic systems as part of a coordinated building-clearance operation.The 22nd edition of India-US joint military exercise Yudh Abhyas is being conducted simultaneously at the Auli Foreign Training Node in Uttarakhand and the Mahajan Field Firing Range in Rajasthan, with 600 personnel from each side participating, according to the ministry of defence.The exercise is aimed at enhancing the two armies' capability to employ Integrated Battle Groups in mountainous and semi-mountainous terrain, with emphasis on infantry-dominated operations. It will also strengthen interoperability through joint planning, coordinated execution and exchanges of operational best practices, the ministry said.Technology infusion is a key focus of the exercise. The Indian Army has said the training will include the employment of drones and autonomous systems for surveillance and reconnaissance, while contemporary weapon systems will be demonstrated at the Mahajan Field Firing Range.The latest counterterrorism drill therefore forms part of a broader exercise combining infantry operations, mountain warfare, unmanned systems, surveillance and emerging battlefield technologies. The simultaneous training at Auli and Mahajan is designed to expose the participating troops to different operational environments while improving interoperability between the two armies.The opening ceremony of Yudh Abhyas 2026 was held at Auli on 15th September , where Major General Amaresh Gunjan, General Officer Commanding, 14 Infantry Division, and Colonel Benjamin Jackman, Commander of the US Army's 1st Infantry Brigade Combat Team, 11th Airborne Division, addressed the participating contingents.
Article Summary: Indian and US soldiers conducted a counterterrorism building-clearance and room- intervention drill at Auli in Uttarakhand on Wednesday. The drill was designed to replicate close-quarter operational situations and demonstrated the coordinated employment of specialised personnel and technology.

Article Title: DUSU polls 2026: DU campuses under tight security as voting begins
Article Text:
djsa





NEW DELHI: Ahead of the DUSU elections 2026, security has been tightened across Delhi University 's North and South campuses on Friday, with more than 2,000 police and paramilitary personnel deployed as students head to polling stations.Polling for the four central panel posts — president, vice-president, secretary and joint secretary — is being conducted in two shifts. Students attending day colleges can vote from 8.30 am to 1 pm, while voting at evening colleges will continue from 3 pm to 7.30 pm.A senior police officer said security arrangements had been put in place around all colleges and other important locations to ensure peaceful polling and maintain law and order.Police personnel have been positioned at key points, while foot patrols, motorcycle teams and PCR vans are maintaining a visible presence around the campuses. Paramilitary forces have also been deployed at strategic locations as part of the security arrangements.Additional security has been deployed around polling centres to manage student movement, prevent overcrowding and check unauthorised gatherings or clashes.Police teams are also monitoring sensitive and vulnerable areas where a large number of students and supporters are expected to gather.The university has restricted vehicular movement on key stretches, including Chhatra Marg, Probyn Road and University Road. The restrictions will remain in force on Friday and Saturday until the results are declared.Police are coordinating with university and college authorities on entry and exit points, movement of students and other arrangements related to polling and counting.The election has major student organisations in the fray, including the RSS-affiliated Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ( ABVP ), Congress-backed National Students' Union of India ( NSUI ) and the AISA-SFI Left alliance.In the 2025 elections, ABVP won three of the four central panel posts, including president, while NSUI won the vice-president's post.Counting will be held on Saturday at the Multipurpose Hall of the University Sports Stadium in North Campus. Police personnel will remain deployed during counting to ensure the process and declaration of results take place peacefully.
Article Summary: Polling for the four central panel posts — president, vice-president, secretary and joint secretary — is being conducted in two shifts. Students attending day colleges can vote from 8.30 am to 1 pm, while voting at evening colleges will continue from 3 pm to 7.30 pm.

Article Title: After Jantar Mantar setback, AIMPLB plans 3-month national UCC campaign, to take battle to states
Article Text:
(File photo) The All India Muslim Personal Law Board





NEW DELHI: The All India Muslim Personal Law Board ( AIMPLB ) on Thursday postponed its proposed dharna against the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) at Jantar Mantar after Delhi Police denied permission, citing the "likelihood of a large gathering and difficulty in managing the crowd".The Board said it had assured authorities that the demonstration would be peaceful and described assembly and protest as constitutional rights. AIMPLB spokesperson S Q R Ilyas, however, advised supporters planning to travel to Delhi not to proceed, asking them to avoid inconvenience and maintain peace.The demonstration was planned to mark the Delhi launch of the Board's three-month 'Save India, Save Sharia' campaign, also described as its 'Movement for Protection of Constitution and Sharia', to mobilise public opinion on constitutional rights, religious freedom and Muslim personal law.At an "emergency" press conference, president Maulana Khalid Saifullah Rahmani, spokesperson Dr Syed Qasim Rasool Ilyas and general secretary Maulana Mohd Fazlur Rahim Mujaddidi criticised the denial and said the campaign would continue through other democratic and legal means. The Board plans to hold public-awareness programmes and legal conventions in Hyderabad, Mumbai, Kolkata and Bengaluru, besides reaching out to religious leaders of other faiths, civil rights groups and tribal communities.The Board has already taken its opposition to the UCC and Waqf law to court. After Uttarakhand notified its UCC on January 27, 2025, AIMPLB filed a challenge in the Uttarakhand High Court in February. After the Gujarat Assembly passed its UCC Bill in March 2026, the Board announced in April that it would challenge the legislation in the Gujarat High Court.Separately, AIMPLB moved the Supreme Court against the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, filing its petition in April 2025. The plea challenges the amendments on constitutional grounds, including Articles 14, 25 and 26 — the Right to Equality, Freedom of Religion (Individual), and Freedom to Manage Religious Affairs (Group).The Board also announced a comprehensive 'White Paper' documenting what it describes as "discrimination against minorities and violations of constitutional and religious freedoms", besides setting out its legal objections to the Waqf law. Its proposed charter will cover the UCC, religious freedom, protection of waqf properties and religious places, hate crimes, alleged unlawful demolitions and equal enforcement of law. It is to be submitted to President Droupadi Murmu, seeking protection of minority rights under Articles 25 to 30.The police decision came amid renewed scrutiny of restrictions on protests at Jantar Mantar. On Thursday, the Delhi High Court questioned the police over its refusal to allow another proposed protest at the venue and asked how a blanket ban on demonstrations could be justified. The court was hearing a petition concerning a separate proposed protest by the Kshatriya Karni Sena.
Article Summary: The All India Muslim Personal Law Board (AIMPLB) on Thursday postponed its proposed dharna against the Uniform Civil Code. Delhi Police denied permission, citing the "likelihood of a large gathering and difficulty in managing the crowd" The Board said it had assured authorities that the demonstration would be peaceful and described assembly and protest as constitutional rights.
